To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of a CSMA broadcast, multi-trunk network is traffic dependent, that it is not possible to improve performance by dedicating one or more trunks for short message transmission, that it is possible to reduce performance by dedicating a trunk for long message transmission, and that it is possible, in a CSMA broadcast environment, to reduce performance by attaching a host to a port whose transfer rate is significantly slower than the transfer rate to the other ports.
1) the performance of a CSMA broadcast LAN is traffic dependent; and 2) that the performance is degraded when the hosts have significantly different transfer rates to the network.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new second level protocol for a broadcast CSMA network.
the performance of a CSMA broadcast computer network.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the broadcast networks studied is dependent upon the relative speeds of the host/ports, the relative speeds of host to host message transfer, and the message length distribution.
a CSMA broadcast protocol is not an effective way to provide a network for short to very long messages.
the network performance is highly sensitive to the host/adapter transfer rate and that the network is not a good candidate for a high performance broadcast network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CSMA is a viable protocol for a broadcast network, and that it is not necessary to use a separate trunk for long message transmission, or to have a host with a very fast transfer rate to a port.
the performance of a CSMA broadcast LAN depends critically on the nature of the host to port transfer rates.

a CSMA broadcast protocol, with a second level protocol that provides a high degree of fairness, is a viable solution for a network of hosts that are all of the same type and have a relatively high speed host to port interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the network performance is not a simple function of the number of hosts, trunks, or trunk capacity.
a broadcast CSMA network can be very sensitive to host to port speed differences, and can be prone to congestion even when the network is underloaded.
the design of the second level of a broadcast network is very critical to performance and that it should not be taken for granted that a broadcast network is necessarily a good choice for a network.
